title: Charge on a Fermat conductor
W: Put a unit of electric charge on a perfectly conducting solid x^4+y^4+z^4 <= 1. Show that the surface charge is thinnest exactly at the six flat points (+-1,0,0),... and thickest exactly at the eight points in the diagonal directions.
M: Let $K=\{x^4+y^4+z^4\le1\}\subset\mathbb R^3$ and let $\mu=\rho\,d\sigma$ be its Newtonian (capacitary) equilibrium measure, $\sigma$ surface measure on $\partial K$ ($\rho$ is real-analytic and positive since $\partial K$ is analytic). Prove that $\min_{\partial K}\rho$ is attained exactly at $(\pm1,0,0),(0,\pm1,0),(0,0,\pm1)$ and $\max_{\partial K}\rho$ exactly at $3^{-1/4}(\pm1,\pm1,\pm1)$.
why: It is folklore that charge accumulates where a conductor is more curved, but the density is nonlocal and only exactly known for ellipsoids (where it is proportional to K^{1/4}). The Fermat superball is the simplest smooth convex body that is not an ellipsoid and has flat points; here Gaussian curvature K=9x^2y^2z^2/(x^6+y^6+z^6)^2 even vanishes along three whole great curves, so rho cannot be a function of K, and a proof needs a genuinely nonlocal comparison argument.
notes: Question is about where the extremes of the equilibrium density sit, not about a quantity. A max/min ratio would be an arbitrary number for one body. No bound formulation.

title: Quintic Szego growth
W: The cubic Szego equation on the circle is completely integrable, and Gerard-Grellier showed that its smooth solutions can have Sobolev norms that are unbounded in time. Decide whether the quintic Szego equation, which is presumably not integrable, also has smooth solutions with unbounded high Sobolev norms.
M: On $L^2_+(\mathbb T)=\{u\in L^2:\hat u(k)=0\ \forall k<0\}$ with Szego projector $\Pi$, consider $i\partial_tu=\Pi(|u|^4u)$, which is globally well posed in $H^s_+$, $s>1/2$, with conserved $\|u\|_{L^2}$, $(Du,u)$ and $\|u\|_{L^6}$. Decide whether there exist $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T)\cap L^2_+$ and $s>1/2$ with $\limsup_{t\to\infty}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}=\infty$.
why: Unbounded Sobolev growth (weak turbulence) is proven almost only for integrable models such as cubic Szego, using their Lax pairs. The quintic Szego equation keeps the same conservation laws and the H^{1/2} bound but loses integrability, so it is a clean model for asking whether turbulent cascades survive without integrable structure, in the spirit of Bourgain's question for NLS.
notes: Natural quantity: the growth rate of ||u(t)||_{H^s}. But I found no reliable current bounds for quintic Szego, and the literature check is still missing. Not converted.

title: Burgers with degenerate critical dissipation
W: Critical half-Laplacian dissipation keeps Burgers smooth. Let that dissipation switch off quadratically at one point of the circle. Do shocks form there?
M: Let $a(x)=1-\cos x$ and consider $u_t+uu_x+\Lambda^{1/2}\big(a\,\Lambda^{1/2}u\big)=0$ on $\mathbb{T}$, $\Lambda=(-\partial_x^2)^{1/2}$. Decide whether every real $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb{T})$ yields a global smooth solution.
why: The question tests whether the Kiselev-Nazarov-Shterenberg regularity mechanism for critical Burgers survives a degenerate, spatially varying coefficient.
notes: Scaling shows the dissipation stays lower order at the Burgers shock scale for any power-law degeneracy |x|^gamma, gamma>0. So no threshold exponent to turn into a bound problem, and no honest fix to B.

title: Drum tones of superellipses
W: Take the region |x|^p + |y|^p <= r^p, scaled to have area 1. At p = 2 it is a disk, which has the lowest possible bass note of any region of that area (Faber–Krahn). As p grows to infinity it becomes a square, whose note is higher. Show that the note rises steadily the whole way from p = 2 to infinity.
M: For $p\in[2,\infty)$ let $D_p=\{(x,y):|x|^p+|y|^p\le r_p^p\}$ with $r_p$ chosen so that $|D_p|=1$, and let $\lambda_1(p)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on $D_p$. Prove that $\lambda_1$ is strictly increasing on $[2,\infty)$, with $\lambda_1(2)=\pi j_{0,1}^2$ and $\lambda_1(p)\uparrow2\pi^2$ as $p\to\infty$.
why: This is a test case for how the Dirichlet eigenvalue moves along a natural one-parameter family of convex sets joining the Faber–Krahn minimiser (the disk) to the square. Monotonicity along such families is a known hard type of question in shape optimisation, since Hadamard's formula gives the derivative but not its sign.
notes: A monotonicity statement whose endpoint values are already known exactly, so there is no gap to bound. Extending to p in [1,2] or higher dimensions keeps it narrow. No honest lift to B.

title: Thue–Morse Lorenz knots
W: Turn the first 2^n letters of the Thue–Morse word into a periodic orbit of the Lorenz flow, and so into a knot K_n. For n >= 4 these knots appear to be hyperbolic. Their volume grows only in proportion to n, the logarithm of the word length, not in proportion to the length itself. Prove that, and find the constant.
M: Let $K_n$ be the Lorenz knot with Lorenz word $t_0t_1\cdots t_{2^n-1}$ (the length-$2^n$ Thue–Morse prefix, $0\mapsto x$, $1\mapsto y$; this word is primitive, since Thue–Morse is overlap-free and $t_{[0,2^n)}=w\bar w$). Prove that $S^3\setminus K_n$ is hyperbolic for all $n\ge4$ and that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{vol}(S^3\setminus K_n)/n$ exists and is positive. Determine the limit.
why: Lorenz knots, the periodic orbits of the Lorenz flow, are positive braids, so their volumes are tightly constrained. Asking how volume depends on the combinatorics of the generating word tests the bridge between symbolic dynamics and hyperbolic geometry. A self-similar word like Thue–Morse should yield a self-similar geometric decomposition, so the volume growth could plausibly be computed exactly.
notes: Natural quantity: lim vol/n, about 8 numerically. No rigorous bounds known (no volume bounds for Lorenz knots pinned down, no literature check). The Thue-Morse family is arbitrary, so no honest lift to B.

title: Shifted Fujita equation
W: In the plane, every positive solution of u_t = Delta u + u^2 blows up (u^2 is exactly Fujita-critical in dimension 2). Does this survive when u^2 is replaced by the product of the values of u one unit to the left and one unit to the right?
M: Let $e=(1,0)$. Prove or disprove: for every $0\le u_0\in C_c(\mathbb R^2)$ with $u_0\not\equiv0$, the solution of $u_t=\Delta u+u(x-e,t)\,u(x+e,t)$ on $\mathbb R^2$ blows up in finite time.
why: This tests how robust the Fujita phenomenon is at the critical exponent p=1+2/n when the nonlinearity is non-local in space. It is a small model of delayed or shifted interactions.
notes: The shift costs only a constant factor, so the critical Fujita proof carries over. Moving or growing shifts also look routine. No natural open quantity and no honest lift to B.

title: Wind-driven fire confinement threshold
quantity: sigma*(a,b): infimum of barrier construction speeds that can confine a fire spreading with speed profile rho(theta)=a+b cos(theta)
lower: sigma*(a,b) >= Lambda*(a-b), Lambda ~ 1.62621 (isotropic lower bound, arXiv 2610.36919, Thm 4.1). Proof: F contains the disc of radius a-b. Bressan's comparison lemma moves blocking from F to that disc, and rescaling time reduces to unit speed.
upper: sigma*(a,b) <= 2 max_{theta in [0,pi]} (a+b cos theta) sin theta (Bressan, Thm 5, non-isotropic case; applies because rho is even and nonincreasing on [0,pi]). This equals 2a at b=0 and tends to (3 sqrt3/2) a as b->a.
W: A fire spreads from a point, faster downwind: speed a + b cos(theta) in direction theta (0<=b<a). Firefighters build a barrier at speed sigma. Let sigma*(a,b) be the smallest speed that can confine the fire. Known: 1.626(a-b) <= sigma* <= 2 max (a+b cos theta) sin theta. Improve either bound, especially in the strong-wind limit b/a -> 1, where the lower bound tends to 0 but the upper bound stays near 2.6a.
M: With $F=\{r(\cos\theta,\sin\theta):0\le r\le a+b\cos\theta\}$ (convexified if $b>a/2$), $R_0=\{0\}$, and Bressan-admissible barriers ($\mathcal H^1(\gamma(t))\le\sigma t$), let $\sigma^*(a,b)$ be the infimum of the $\sigma$ that allow bounded $\bigcup_tR(t)$. Known: $\Lambda(a-b)\le\sigma^*\le2\max_{\theta}(a+b\cos\theta)\sin\theta$ with $\Lambda\approx1.6262$. Prove $\liminf_{b\to a}\sigma^*(a,b)/a>0$, or improve either bound for some fixed $b/a\in(0,1)$.
why: This is the anisotropic version of Bressan's fire confinement problem. Wind is the realistic case. The only lower bound comes from comparison with the upwind (slowest) speed, so it collapses in strong wind, while the upper bound comes from the crosswind width. Whether confinement cost scales with the crosswind width or the upwind speed is a clean, checkable question. For each fixed b, it contains the open isotropic gap (b=0).
notes: I derived the lower bound myself by comparison and scaling, not from the literature. I found no anisotropic necessary condition published. Grade B, not A: it derives from the famous isotropic problem, and the strong-wind regime may give way to a simple width argument.

title: KdV with a cosine coefficient
W: Put a cos x in front of the cubic term of the modified KdV equation on the circle. The energy and the mean are still conserved, but the L² norm is not, and the energy no longer has a definite sign. Can smooth solutions blow up in finite time?
M: Consider $u_t+u_{xxx}+(\cos(x)\,u^3)_x=0$ on $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$ with real $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T)$. It is Hamiltonian, $u_t=\partial_x\frac{\delta H}{\delta u}$ with $H=\int(\tfrac12u_x^2-\tfrac14\cos(x)u^4)$, and conserves $\int u$ and $H$. However, $\frac{d}{dt}\int u^2=\frac12\int\sin(x)u^4$. Decide whether every such $u_0$ yields a global smooth solution, or whether $\|u(t)\|_{H^1}\to\infty$ in finite time for some $u_0$.
why: Standard mKdV on the torus is globally well-posed because L² conservation and the L²-subcritical Gagliardo–Nirenberg inequality control the energy. A spatially varying coefficient breaks the translation symmetry and so the L² law, which removes the a priori bound. Any blow-up would have to come from L² growth rather than L² concentration. That is a mechanism of real interest for inhomogeneous dispersive equations, and this is about the simplest model where it could occur.
notes: Asks whether blow-up happens. There is no natural constant or exponent with known bounds, and the literature check is incomplete.

title: Hat Ising universality
W: Magnets on a hat tiling should behave at their critical point exactly like magnets on a square grid. Prove it.
M: Let $G$ be the planar graph whose vertices are the tiles of a fixed hat tiling (Smith–Myers–Kaplan–Goodman-Strauss), with edges between tiles sharing a boundary segment. Consider the ferromagnetic nearest-neighbour Ising model on $G$ with uniform coupling $J=1$. Prove that there is a critical $\beta_c$ (independent of the tiling in the hull), and that as $\beta\to\beta_c$ the spontaneous magnetization, susceptibility and correlation length obey $M(\beta)\asymp(\beta-\beta_c)^{1/8}$, $\chi(\beta)\asymp|\beta-\beta_c|^{-7/4}$, $\xi(\beta)\asymp|\beta-\beta_c|^{-1}$.
why: Rigorous 2D Ising universality is known for isoradial graphs at Z-invariant weights and for periodic graphs. Uniform couplings on an aperiodic, non-isoradial graph are not covered. The hat graph is a canonical such test, and numerics (Matsubara–Suzuki) support universality.
notes: The content is exact exponents (universality), not a bound. Rigorous bounds on beta_c for the hat graph would be a narrow side quantity with no literature beyond numerics.

title: Largest prime factor of Markov numbers
W: Markov numbers are the numbers appearing in positive integer solutions of x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz. Show that the largest prime factor of a Markov number tends to infinity. Equivalently, for any finite set of primes, only finitely many Markov numbers are built from those primes alone.
M: Let $\mathcal M=\{m\ge1:\exists\,x,y\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\ x^2+y^2+m^2=3xym\}$ and let $P(m)$ denote the largest prime factor of $m$ (with $P(1)=1$). Prove that $P(m)\to\infty$ as $m\to\infty$ in $\mathcal M$; equivalently, for every finite set $S$ of primes, only finitely many $m\in\mathcal M$ are $S$-units.
why: Corvaja and Zannier used the Subspace Theorem to show that the greatest prime factor of the product xy over Markov pairs tends to infinity. The single-number version is the natural strengthening. It sits next to the uniqueness conjecture, where Markov numbers that are prime powers are already handled, and to recent strong-approximation work on the Markoff surface.
notes: A quantitative version (P(m) >= f(m)) has no known lower bound at all, so it is the same open problem. Counting S-unit Markov numbers gives no meaningful bound. Not converted.

title: Jacobi matrix of primes
W: Build an infinite tridiagonal (Jacobi) matrix with zero diagonal and the primes 2, 3, 5, 7, ... on the off-diagonals. The standard criteria for purely absolutely continuous spectrum need the off-diagonal sequence to vary regularly, and they just fail because prime gaps fluctuate. Decide whether the spectrum is nevertheless purely absolutely continuous on the whole real line.
M: Let $J$ be the self-adjoint Jacobi operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ given by $(Ju)_n=p_{n-1}u_{n-1}+p_nu_{n+1}$ (with $p_0u_0:=0$), where $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime. It is self-adjoint by Carleman's criterion, since $\sum1/p_n=\infty$. Decide whether $\sigma(J)=\sigma_{ac}(J)=\mathbb R$ with no singular part.
why: Unbounded Jacobi matrices with weights $a_n\to\infty$ and $b_n=0$ have purely absolutely continuous spectrum under bounded-variation conditions on $a_{n+1}/a_n$ (Janas-Naboko, Clark). For the primes, the variation of $p_{n+1}/p_n$ diverges like $\sum g_n/p_n$. A Prüfer heuristic suggests the real obstruction is the oscillatory series $\sum(-1)^n g_n/p_n\,e^{i\phi_n}$ ($g_n$ the prime gaps), so the spectral type appears to encode a parity-of-index statistic of prime gaps.
notes: Possible quantity: the exponent theta in A_N = sum (-1)^n g_n = O(N^theta). This reduces to fluctuations of the alternating prime sum, and I could not pin down reliable current bounds. The spectral question is the real content.
